title: Generative AI Adoption
description: Share of U.S. working-age adults (18–64) using generative AI at work, from a nationally representative quarterly survey (Real-Time Population Survey). Work adoption (40.7%) lags overall use (55.9%), consistent with workers adopting ahead of their employers. Overall adoption has outpaced both the PC and internet at comparable points post-launch.

proxyContext.actualUnit: % of Python code on GitHub that is AI-assisted
proxyContext.rationale: AI-assisted code share as proxy for developer AI adoption at work

sources.title: The State of Consumer AI. Part 1 - Usage
sources.excerpt: Today, AI apps have crossed 1 billion weekly active users and ChatGPT alone accounts for 900M of that.

sources.title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI
sources.excerpt: Nationally representative survey of 25,000+ working-age adults finds generative AI adoption reached 55.9% overall and 40.7% at work by November 2025, outpacing PC and internet adoption at comparable points post-launch.

sources.title: GenAI Adoption Tracker (Harvard / St. Louis Fed)
sources.excerpt: Quarterly dashboard tracking generative AI adoption among U.S. working-age adults. Feb & May 2025 values estimated from tracker chart; all other values from published working paper.

sources.title: January 2026 US Labor Market Update: Jobs Mentioning AI Are Growing Amid Broader Hiring Weakness
sources.excerpt: Only about 43% of US workers reported regularly using AI at work last year

sources.title: Beyond Productivity: Measuring the Real Value of AI
sources.excerpt: 85% of employees report saving one to seven hours per week using AI. Employees who use AI every day are overwhelmingly optimistic – more than 90% believe it will help them succeed.

sources.title: Elevating Human Potential: The AI Skills Revolution
sources.excerpt: almost two-thirds (59%) say their department is currently using AI while one-third (31%) of respondents are experimenting with its use

sources.title: Your New Job Is to Onboard AI Agents: How AI Native Companies Actually Operate
sources.excerpt: PMs and marketers should default to an AI interface. These functions should be doing 80-100% of their work through a chat interface.

sources.title: AI Skills Improve Job Prospects: Causal Evidence from a Hiring Experiment
sources.excerpt: AI skills significantly increase interview invitation probabilities by approximately 8 to 15 percentage points, compared with candidates without such skills

sources.title: Will Artificial Intelligence Get in the Way of Achieving Gender Equality?
sources.publisher: NHH Norwegian School of Economics (Carvajal, Franco, Isaksson)
sources.excerpt: Among 595 business school students in Norway, male students were 25 percent more likely to be high AI users, and the gap was widest among the highest-performing women.

sources.title: What do professional software developers need to know to succeed in an age of Artificial Intelligence?
sources.excerpt: We describe our research with 21 developers at the cutting edge of using AI

sources.title: Survey evidence on gen AI and households: job prospects amid trust concerns
sources.excerpt: Almost half of US households use generative artificial intelligence tools. Average expected probability of higher productivity: 30%; of job loss: 13%.

sources.title: Americans are increasingly skeptical about AI's effects
sources.excerpt: 56% of Americans use AI tools; 28% weekly. Skepticism about AI's effects increased 8 percentage points year over year.

sources.title: 2025 Work Trend Index
sources.excerpt: 75% of knowledge workers use AI at work. 78% bring their own AI tools. Survey of 31,000 workers across 31 countries.

sources.title: GenAI Adoption Patterns
sources.excerpt: About 20% use AI professionally; 57% personal use. Adoption varies significantly by education and income.

sources.title: Gender Gap in AI Adoption
sources.excerpt: Gender gap in AI adoption: women adopt less; 5.3 percentage point gap in UK data.

sources.title: Who is using AI to code? Global diffusion and impact of generative AI
sources.excerpt: AI-assisted coding jumped from around 5% in 2022 to nearly 30% in Q4 2024.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot in UK Civil Service
sources.excerpt: GitHub Copilot saves 26 minutes per day across 20,000 UK civil servants.

sources.title: State of AI in the Enterprise: The untapped edge
sources.excerpt: Workforce access to AI has expanded by 50% in just one year—growing from under 40% to under 60% of workers now equipped with sanctioned AI tools.

sources.title: AI use by individuals surges across the OECD as adoption by firms continues to expand
sources.excerpt: 36.8% of individuals across OECD used generative AI in 2025. 20.2% of firms used AI in 2025 (up from 8.7% in 2023). 41.1% of employed individuals used generative AI. 52.0% of large firms vs 17.4% small.

sources.title: The State of Generative AI Adoption in 2025
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.excerpt: 23% of employed workers used generative AI at work weekly as of late 2024. Share of work hours with GenAI increased from 4.1% (Nov 2024) to 5.7% (Aug 2025). GenAI may have increased aggregate labor productivity by up to 1.3%.
